one-check-per-line.why: all 2 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 2

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 2 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: I checked the verifier's PASS/FAIL conditions against each expect line. Check 2 is fine: a README mention of --tsv that says what the flag does matches "documents --tsv". Check 1 is not. Its PASS requires "both commands exit 0 every time", and its FAIL triggers when "either command exits non-zero". Expect line 1 only asks that --tsv read tab input on stdin and print the same JSON array as the plain command. It says nothing about exit status. Check 1 also requires a set output shape, "a JSON array of objects keyed by the header row", with a literal example. The words only require the --tsv output to match whatever the plain CSV command prints, not that it has a given structure. Both requirements are stricter than the expect line and belong under Advisory, not in PASS/FAIL.

runs-as-written.why:
The criterion is met: every command in both briefs would run as written in this repository. Builder brief: the files it reads and edits (bin/csv2json.js, src/parse.js, test/csv.test.js, README.md) are all tracked. `npm test` runs the existing "node --test" script, which picks up test/*.test.js files. The README line `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv` is example text to add, not a command to run. Verifier brief: the `printf '...	...' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv > /tmp/tsv.out; echo "exit $?"` pipelines are valid shell, and the plain CSV pipeline is too. `cmp /tmp/tsv.out /tmp/csv.out && cat /tmp/csv.out` compares files made by the commands before it. `grep -n -- '--tsv' README.md` puts `--` before the pattern, so grep doesn't read `--tsv` as an option. The single-column `printf 'a
1
2
'` repeat and the advisory commands are also valid. The `--tsv` flag itself is added by the builder before the verifier runs.

catches-traps.why: I checked all three must_catch items. Item 1 holds: the builder brief says "keep the current comma behaviour exactly as it is" and "Run `npm test` and confirm every test passes." Item 3 holds: Check 1 pipes the same table as TSV and as CSV, then runs `cmp /tmp/tsv.out /tmp/csv.out`, and repeats this with a second table. Item 2 holds only in part. The Advisory section sits outside PASS/FAIL and suggests "Run npm test and report the result", plus a CSV regression check. But it never says that no expect line covers CSV behaviour or npm test. The heading "(not part of PASS or FAIL)" only marks the items as ungraded. It doesn't point out the coverage gap, which item 2 requires. So the briefs don't handle every must_catch item.

avoids-must-not.why: The verifier brief has two checks, one for each expect line. Neither check's PASS or FAIL condition needs npm test or the CSV tests to pass. Check 1 depends only on exit codes, `cmp` showing the --tsv and CSV outputs match, and the JSON array's shape. Check 2 depends only on `grep -n -- '--tsv' README.md` and the text around it. npm test and the plain-CSV check appear only under "Advisory (not part of PASS or FAIL)", and the brief only asks the verifier to report on them. Neither one can decide the verdict, so the advisory list does not count as a third check. The builder brief has the builder run npm test, but the must_not list only limits the verifier's checks and the conditions for lines 1 and 2, so this is allowed. None of the must_not items is broken.

methods-private.why:
I compared the builder brief against each verifier check. Check 1 uses tables the builder never sees: the 'name	age	city' table, a single-column table and the cmp comparison. Check 2's `grep -n -- '--tsv' README.md` and its PASS/FAIL wording don't appear in the builder brief either. The builder's step 3 tells it to write its own test with 'a	b
1	2
' → '[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]
', and the rule allows the builder to write its own tests. The verifier's advisory example looks similar ('a,b
1,2
' piped to the plain command). But that is comma input to the plain command, not tab input to the --tsv command, and it isn't a PASS/FAIL condition, so it's a different probe. The builder is told to run `npm test`, which is allowed. The builder brief gives no PASS or FAIL conditions. The criterion holds.
